subject: Clarify: backup snapshot retention / erasure timeline for DPA redline
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acmehealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: backup copies & onshore copy erasure timeline

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. We're reviewing the DPA redlines and have a couple of specific asks around backups and onshore copies before legal signs off. Two items in particular:

1) Backup / snapshot purge timing: Acme's security team expects documented evidence that customer data will be removed from backups within a defined window after an erasure request. Our current procurement policy prefers a 90-day maximum for purged backups. Can you confirm Redwood's standard timeline and whether that is negotiable?

2) Onshore compliance copies: For certain regulated datasets we need an onshore snapshot retained for 180 days for audit response. Can Redwood support an exception for an onshore copy that is retained longer than the standard backup window, subject to controls (encryption, limited access, and auditable approval)?

I've attached our latest questionnaire and a draft set of redlines (see AcmeHealth_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx). Can your team propose explicit contract language we can insert into Appendix C (Backups & Snapshots)? Also please include what deletion evidence you can provide (log extract, certificate of erasure, SOC2 artifact).

Best,
Sara
Sara Lopez
Head of Security & Compliance
Acme Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: backup copies & onshore copy erasure timeline

Hi Sara — appreciate the clear asks and the redline draft. Summary answers up front, then proposed contract text below.

Summary:
- Standard: primary-data erasure completed within 30 days of a validated request; encrypted backups/snapshots subject to a 90-day purge window.
- Exception: we can support a controlled onshore snapshot held up to 180 days for compliance with documented customer approval and an explicit Appendix C exception (audit logs + limited access controls).
- Evidence: we can provide an "Erase Certificate" (machine-generated manifest) and a scoped audit log extract showing the purge job and object tombstones. We can also reference SOC 2 Type II controls that govern our backup retention and deletion processes.

Proposed appendix redline (suggested language for Appendix C, Backup & Snapshot Exceptions):
"Appendix C — Backup and Snapshot Retention.
Primary copies of Customer Data will be deleted or returned within thirty (30) days following Customer's verified erasure request. Backups and snapshots containing Customer Data shall be retained only as long as necessary for redundancy and recovery and shall be scheduled for purge within ninety (90) days of the erasure request, subject to the following carve-out: upon written request and documented approval by Customer, Redwood may retain a single, encrypted onshore snapshot of Customer Data for audit or regulatory compliance purposes for a maximum period of one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of approval. Access to such onshore snapshots will be restricted to named personnel, protected by encryption at rest, and logged for audit purposes. Redwood will provide a machine-generated Erasure Certificate and a purge audit log extract to Customer upon completion of the purge."

I'll attach a cleaned-up draft (Redwood_Proposed_DPA_AppendixC_redline.docx) and can route this to Legal for a quick review. Monica/Rishi — can you confirm operational feasibility and whether we need any additional controls (HSM key separation, transfer logs) for the onshore snapshot carve-out?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acmehealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: contracts@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-22T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: backup copies & onshore copy erasure timeline

Laura — this is helpful, thank you. A few quick follow-ups: 

- The proposed Appendix C language is aligned with our expectations. One request: can Redwood commit to providing the Erasure Certificate within five (5) business days after completion of the purge? Our compliance team needs the evidence on a short timeline for audits.

- For the onshore snapshot carve-out, we need two additional items documented: (1) a named-approver workflow (email trail or DocuSign) that authorizes the retention, and (2) a retention access matrix showing who can decrypt/access the snapshot.

We can accept the 180-day maximum if those two items are included. I'll send this to contracts for a small amendment; please expect a DocuSign envelope for the Appendix C approval flow once your legal team signs off.

Attachments: AcmeHealth_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx (redlines inline)

Regards,
Sara

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: backup copies & onshore copy erasure timeline — proposed sign-off items

Sara — thanks, and good to hear we're aligned. Quick operational confirmations from our side: 

1) Erasure Certificate timing: agreed — Redwood will generate and deliver the Erasure Certificate and purge audit extract within five (5) business days after the purge job completes. We will include a job id and object tombstone marker for traceability.

2) Named-approver workflow: we can implement a DocuSign-based approval for the onshore snapshot retention; the DocuSign record will serve as the documented approval referenced in Appendix C. Please confirm the signers (we suggest Acme's Head of Compliance + Redwood's Customer Security lead).

3) Access matrix & controls: operationally, onshore snapshots will be encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys where available; access will be restricted to named personnel (we will produce an access matrix and KMS key policy excerpt as part of the amendment). If Acme requires HSM-backed key separation, Aditya, can you weigh in on feasibility and estimated lead time?

Next steps: 
- Laura/Redwood to circulate the redlined Appendix C (attached) to Redwood Legal this afternoon.
- Acme to send the DocuSign envelope with named approvers.
- Redwood to confirm HSM/key-separation feasibility if requested (Aditya to follow up by 2027-04-28).

I'll loop in Legal after this note. If that sequence works for you, we should be able to finalize the DPA amendment next week.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_DPA_AppendixC_redline.docx]
